descricao: Prompts prontos para gerar podcast, vídeo, slides, quiz, flashcards, infográfico, mapa mental e diálogo a partir de qualquer material.

secoes.conteudo:
Cole qualquer um dos materiais de inglês como fonte no NotebookLM. Depois, volte aqui, copie o prompt do formato que quiser e cole no NotebookLM.

Cada prompt garante três coisas: cobertura total do conteúdo, inglês em nível A2–B1 e linguagem envolvente — não uma lista chata de palavras.

Fluxo sugerido: comece pelo **Podcast** — cole o prompt no campo Customize do Audio Overview antes de gerar. Para todos os outros formatos, use o chat do NotebookLM: cole o prompt, aguarde a resposta e leve o resultado para a ferramenta final (Canva, Anki, Gamma, Miro...).

No NotebookLM: clique em **Audio Overview** → **Customize** → cole o prompt abaixo → clique em Generate.

```
Create a podcast between two hosts who are genuinely enthusiastic about learning English. Both hosts speak at an intermediate level (A2–B1): clear, natural sentences, real-world examples.

Rules:
- Cover EVERY vocabulary item and concept in the material — no skipping
- Never just define a word — use it in a vivid, relatable example sentence
- When two words are similar or often confused, make it a small debate or "aha moment"
- For false friends and grammar traps, react with genuine surprise or humor
- Include at least one memorable story, analogy, or real-life situation per section
- End with the 3–4 things a listener must remember after this episode
- Tone: two curious friends, never two textbook narrators
- Keep sentences short. Keep energy high. No filler phrases.
```

No NotebookLM: abra o **chat** → cole o prompt abaixo → copie o roteiro gerado para usar com CapCut, HeyGen ou gravar direto na câmera.

```
Write a video script based on this material based on this material. The presenter speaks directly to the viewer. Cover every vocabulary item and concept — however long that takes.

Requirements:
- Open with a relatable situation or question that hooks the viewer — no "Hello everyone, today we will learn..."
- English at A2–B1 level: natural, conversational, never robotic
- - For each key word or concept: one clear definition + one vivid example sentence
- Add [PAUSE] where the viewer should think or repeat the word out loud
- Add [SHOW: word / example] where text should appear on screen
- For contrasting words (e.g. slim vs thin), structure it as a mini-challenge: "Which one would you use here?"
- Close with an encouraging line that makes the viewer want to practice right now
- Tone: knowledgeable friend, not classroom lecture
```

No NotebookLM: abra o **chat** → cole o prompt abaixo → use o resultado como base no Canva, Gamma ou Google Slides.

```
Generate a slide-by-slide outline for a presentation based on this material. Cover every vocabulary item and concept — however many slides that takes.

For each slide, provide:
- Title: short and punchy
- Content: bullet points in English at A2–B1 level — as many as needed, clear and concise
- Example: one natural example sentence or usage note

Structure:
- First slide: hook — a relatable question or situation (no "Today we will learn")
- One slide per section of the material, plus extra slides as needed for vocabulary contrasts
- Final slide: key takeaways — the most important things to remember

Tone: conversational and visual. No bullet should read like a dictionary entry.
```

No NotebookLM: abra o **chat** → cole o prompt abaixo → use as perguntas para estudar ou monte um formulário no Google Forms.

```
Create a quiz based on this material for an A2–B1 English learner. Cover every vocabulary item and concept — however many questions that takes.

Mix these question types:
- Fill-in-the-blank sentences using vocabulary from the material
- "Which word fits better?" questions with two similar words
- True/false questions about meaning or usage
- Translation challenges: Portuguese to English, using the vocabulary covered

After each question, add the correct answer and a one-sentence explanation of why.
Tone: encouraging. If the answer requires nuance, explain it briefly and clearly.
```

No NotebookLM: abra o **chat** → cole o prompt abaixo → importe o resultado no Anki ou Quizlet.

```
Generate flashcards based on this material. Every key vocabulary item must appear — however many cards that takes.

Format for each card:
FRONT: [word or phrase in English] — [one-sentence context clue, not a definition]
BACK: [meaning in Portuguese] + [one example sentence in English at A2–B1 level]

Rules:
- Context clue on the front should hint at the meaning without giving it away
- Example sentence on the back must feel natural, not textbook
- For false friends, add a ⚠️ note on the back explaining the trap
- For words with a confusable pair, create one card per word and cross-reference them
- No card should repeat an example from another card
```

No NotebookLM: abra o **chat** → cole o prompt abaixo → monte o infográfico no Canva usando a estrutura gerada.

```
Design a text layout for an infographic about this material, ready to be built in Canva or similar.

Structure:
- Title: one short, catchy headline
- Sections covering all content: each with a section title + items (word + ultra-short definition)
- One "Watch Out!" box highlighting the most important false friend or common mistake
- One "Quick Rule" box with the key grammar or usage tip from the material
- One "Remember This Pair" box comparing two easily confused words
- Footer: one motivating sentence for the learner

Visual tone: clean, modern, friendly. No full sentences in the main sections — keywords and short labels only. Think poster, not essay.
```

No NotebookLM: abra o **chat** → cole o prompt abaixo → importe o resultado como lista indentada no Miro, Notion ou XMind.

```
Create a mind map outline for this material.

Central node: the topic title

Branch structure:
- One main branch per section of the material
- Each branch has leaf nodes covering all key vocabulary and concepts in that section
- Where two words contrast, connect them with a double arrow and label it "opposite"
- Where a word is a false friend, mark it with ⚠️
- Where a grammar rule applies, add it as a standalone leaf with a 📌 marker

Output as indented text (can be imported into Miro, Notion, or XMind). No full sentences — nodes only.
```

No NotebookLM: abra o **chat** → cole o prompt abaixo → use o diálogo para leitura em voz alta, roleplay ou análise de vocabulário em contexto.

```
Write a natural conversation between two people (Alex and Sam) that uses every key vocabulary item from this material at least once.

Rules:
- Setting: a realistic, everyday situation — pick the most natural fit for the topic
- English at A2–B1 level: short turns, natural rhythm, contractions
- Each vocabulary word should appear in a realistic context, never forced
- After the dialogue, add a "Spot the vocabulary" section: list every key word that appeared and the exact line where it was used
- Tone: warm and natural, like something you'd actually hear between two people
```
